customManagers.description: The PDF renderer lock names the Buildx client by version and the commit its tag points to. The depName matches the workflow input, so both land in one pull request.

packageRules.description: Keep GitHub Action updates together for one review. Tool versions passed as workflow inputs stay out of the group.
A tool version passed as a workflow input is bound to a lock outside the workflow: Python to the fixture-019 environment, Buildx to the PDF renderer lock.
prBodyNotes: This repository binds workflow tool versions to locks: Python to the fixture-019 environment, Buildx to the PDF renderer lock. `npm run validate:policy` fails until a bound value moves together with its lock in this pull request.

packageRules.description: The custom manager moves the renderer lock's Buildx version and revision with the workflow inputs. The values derived from the lock still move by hand in the same pull request.
prBodyNotes: This update moves the Buildx version and revision in `tooling/pdf-renderer/lock.json`. Before merge, recompute the BuildKit authority digest in `tooling/pdf-tools/contract.json`, `tooling/clrs-generator/image-contract.json` and `tooling/internal/clrsfixture/image_contract.go`, update the approved value in `scripts/validate-engineering-policy.mjs`, and re-record the book with `npm run generate:book-pdf` (decision 0115).

packageRules.description: Keep npm dependency declarations and the lockfile exact.
Major upgrades require an explicit compatibility review.
Hold TypeScript below 7 until a typescript-eslint release admits TypeScript 7 in its peer range.
Hold ESLint below 10 until eslint-plugin-react and eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y releases admit ESLint 10 in their peer ranges; @eslint/js versions with ESLint.
praetor-managed files: praetorctl adopt ships their updates and praetorctl audit locks them byte for byte
